Patch Notes

4.2.0

A feature release: LPOS gains the SOC 2 Compliance Guild — compliance codified into the operating system, run autonomously, with staged remediation and an evidence trail.

What is new

  • GUILD-038, the SOC 2 Compliance Guild: owns the codified control framework (AICPA

2017 Trust Services Criteria, revised 2022 points of focus) and the autonomous compliance loop. See SOC 2 Compliance Guild.

  • **lpos_engine.compliance**: 21 machine-checkable controls mapped across CC1–CC9 plus

Availability, Confidentiality, and Processing Integrity; every result carries evidence citing the exact files inspected. Type 2 operating effectiveness is computed over a 90-day observation window from the evidence history — controls earn "effective" by passing consistently, not once.

  • SO-025, SOC 2 Compliance Audit (daily): inventory → audit → staged remediation →

report. Fixes for failing controls are built as copies in the staging test environment (~/.hermes/compliance/staging/) so live work is never broken, and adoption into the main system happens only through exact-action Principal approval.

  • The compliance page: ~/.hermes/compliance/report.html — problems, fixes, the

audit log of changes, and project status, in one self-contained HTML page. The dashboard reads compliance/status.json alongside the monitor's health strip.

  • CLI: lpos compliance audit | report | status.

What you will notice

A new daily Standing Operation in lpos list-workflows (25 total), the compliance page appearing under your Hermes root after the first run, and — if the audit finds gaps — staged fixes waiting for your approval rather than surprise changes to live files.
